subject: Social Science
chapter: Chapter 8: Banks and the Magic of Finance
central_question: How do banks, payment systems, financial institutions and stock markets move money, support saving and credit, and contribute to development while requiring regulation and safety?
in_scope_units: Introduction—financial infrastructure as banks, payment systems, stock markets and institutions supporting households, businesses and government.
What banks do—accounts, deposits, withdrawals, saving and borrowing through the Navdeep and Rima example.
Types of bank account—savings, current and fixed deposit accounts.
Interest and compounding—growth of savings and the chessboard story of repeated doubling.
Passbooks, debit and credit—recording financial transactions.
Loans and credit—purposes of borrowing, repayment, interest and the bank’s interest-rate spread.
Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana—wider access, direct transfers and banking inclusion.
Other financial institutions—post-office savings, IFCI and NABARD.
Reserve Bank of India—central bank, banker to banks, currency issue, benchmark rates and regulation.
Historical lending—temple credit and copper-plate agreements.
Payment Modes and Systems—withdrawal slips, ATMs, PINs and account access.
Cheques, POS, internet banking and mobile payments—account-to-account transfers.
Unified Payments Interface—NPCI, QR codes, UPI PIN, cashless payment and international adoption.
Stock Market—shares, stock, investment, BSE, company finance, boom, crash and price fluctuations.
Financial fraud—fake calls, harmful links, OTP and PIN safety, helpline 1930 and cybercrime reporting.
Before we move on and Questions and activities 1–12—financial infrastructure, accounts, compounding, money flow, stock markets, digital safety and practical banking.
banned_topics: Advanced investment advice, stock selection or promises of returns.
Detailed monetary policy beyond the RBI roles and benchmark interest rate named in the chapter.
Cryptocurrency, which is not part of the chapter.
Detailed barter, coinage and market supply chains covered in earlier chapters.

known_pitfalls.claim: Banks store all deposited money without using it.
known_pitfalls.correction: Banks keep reserves and also lend part of deposits to borrowers while paying depositors interest.
Interest grows savings for depositors but increases the amount borrowers must repay; compounding can strengthen either effect.

known_pitfalls.claim: RBI is an ordinary commercial bank for individual savings accounts.
known_pitfalls.correction: RBI is India’s central bank and banker to banks, supervising the system and controlling currency and benchmark rates.

known_pitfalls.claim: A debit card and a credit entry in a passbook mean the same thing.
known_pitfalls.correction: In the chapter’s transaction language, debit is money leaving an account and credit is money entering it; a debit card accesses the holder’s bank funds.

known_pitfalls.claim: UPI payments are safe even when a user shares the UPI PIN or OTP.
known_pitfalls.correction: The chapter warns never to share PINs, passwords, OTPs or sensitive bank information and to report fraud promptly.

known_pitfalls.claim: Buying a share guarantees a profit.
known_pitfalls.correction: Share prices rise and fall with company performance, policy, instability, war and economic shocks, so gains and losses are both possible.
